runbook.title: Runbook: fraud-scoring latency
steps: 1. Check for a recent deploy to risk-rules first: INC-2026-032 was caused by dep:risk-rules-v2.8.0 (RISK-412: lower RULES_CACHE_TTL 300s -> 5s so rule edits apply faster).
2. If risk-rules RULES_CACHE_TTL was changed, roll it back. What fixed INC-2026-032: Priya rolled back RULES_CACHE_TTL to 300s; config-service load recovered
3. Watch config-service CPU and request rate: risk-rules calls config-service at request time; the service catalog does not list this dependency. (fact:learned-risk-rules-config-s…
4. Open the fraud-scoring dashboard and check p99 latency and pod CPU.
5. If CPU is above 70%, scale the deployment up by 50% and wait five minutes.
6. Check the feature store database for slow queries and connection saturation.
7. If latency is still high, restart the pods one at a time.
8. If payments are being declined, ask payments-api on-call to enable the conservative fallback.

matches.title: Slack's Incident on 2-22-22
matches.summary: A rolling Consul agent upgrade restarted memcached nodes at peak and they came back empty. Cache misses turned an expensive membership query into scatter queries across every database shard, and the overloaded database stopped the cache from refilling. Throttling client boots and fixing the query restored service.

matches.title: More Details on Today's Outage
matches.summary: A change to a stored configuration value made an automated checker treat it as invalid, so every client tried to fix its cached copy by querying one database cluster. Errors were read as invalid values and caused more cache deletions, a feedback loop. The site was taken down to stop traffic, then restored gradually.

props.title: risk-rules README
props.text: # risk-rules risk-rules is the fraud rule engine. It evaluates analyst-authored rules (velocity limits, geo mismatches, device reputation, BIN blocklists) against the feature vector that fraud-scoring sends for every payment, and returns a list of rule verdicts in under 20 ms. ## Ownership Owner and primary contact: Arjun Mehta (Risk & Fraud). Page the Risk & Fraud on-call if Arjun is unavailable…
props.flagged_reason: author_left; names_departed_person (Arjun Mehta); old_vs_changes (3 deploys since); missing_learned_dependency (svc:config-service)

props.title: Rule edits take up to 5 minutes to apply — reduce rules cache TTL
props.text: Analysts report that editing a fraud rule in the console takes up to 5 minutes to take effect in production, because risk-rules caches the rule set for RULES_CACHE_TTL (currently 300s). Proposal: reduce RULES_CACHE_TTL from 300s to 5s so edits apply almost immediately. Acceptance criteria: an edited rule is visible to fraud-scoring within 10 seconds. Shipped in risk-rules v2.8.0.

props.title: Postmortem: fraud-scoring timeouts during checkout peak
props.text: INC-2025-031, sev 2. Impact: about 11% of card payments failed or were declined for two hours at the evening checkout peak. Timeline: risk-rules v2.3.0 lowered RULES_CACHE_TTL to 10s. props.title: RULES_CACHE_TTL must stay ≥ 300s
props.rationale: Below ~30s config-service saturates at checkout peak, because risk-rules refetches rulesets from it on every cache miss. This is what caused INC-2025-031.

props.summary: risk-rules v2.3.0 lowered RULES_CACHE_TTL to 10s. At checkout peak every risk-rules pod refetched rulesets, saturating config-service and timing out fraud-scoring. Rolled back the TTL to 300s and added cache warm-up.

props.title: ledger-service connection pool exhausted during payout run
props.summary: ledger-service v3.4.0 added a parallel payout journal writer that opened more connections than the ledger-db pool allowed, starving payment captures. Raised the pool ceiling and capped writer concurrency.
props.symptom: payout run stalled; payment captures failing with pool timeout errors

props.summary: Rolled back TTL to 300s and added cache warm-up
props.steps: 1. Roll back RULES_CACHE_TTL to 300s. 2. Restart risk-rules pods gradually. 3. Add cache warm-up on pod start. 4. Watch config-service CPU until it is below 40%.

nodes.name: Re-enabled local config cache with jittered TTL

props.summary: Re-enabled local config cache with jittered TTL
props.steps: 1. Redeploy merchant-onboarding with the local config cache enabled. 2. Add +/-20% jitter to the cache TTL. 3. Confirm config-service latency returns to normal.

nodes.label: Resolution
nodes.name: Raised pool ceiling and capped payout writer concurrency

props.summary: Raised pool ceiling and capped payout writer concurrency
props.steps: 1. Reduce payout writer concurrency to 4. 2. Raise the ledger-db connection pool limit. 3. Re-run the stalled payout batch.

props.title: Slack's Incident on 2-22-22
props.summary: A rolling Consul agent upgrade restarted memcached nodes at peak and they came back empty. Cache misses turned an expensive membership query into scatter queries across every database shard, and the overloaded database stopped the cache from refilling. Throttling client boots and fixing the query restored service.

props.title: More Details on Today's Outage
props.summary: A change to a stored configuration value made an automated checker treat it as invalid, so every client tried to fix its cached copy by querying one database cluster. Errors were read as invalid values and caused more cache deletions, a feedback loop. The site was taken down to stop traffic, then restored gradually.
